'''''Tulipa greigii''''', ('''Greig's tulip''') is a species of [[Tulipa|tulip]] native to Central Asia and Iran.<ref name="542931-1" >{{cite web |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:542931-1 |title=''Tulipa greigii'' Regel |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=2017 |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=Board of Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=31 August 2020 }}</ref>

==Taxonomy==
The Latin [[Botanical name#Binary name|specific epithet]] ''greigi'' honors the Russian [[Samuel Greig]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Greig's Tulip 'Chopin' |url=http://www.paghat.com/tulipgreigiichopin.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030425122908/http://www.paghat.com/tulipgreigiichopin.html |url-status=usurped |archive-date=April 25, 2003 |publisher=paghat.com |access-date=17 September 2017 }}</ref> (1735–1788, "Father of the Russian navy")<ref name=pacific>{{cite web |title=Tulipa Species Two |date=13 May 2015 |url=http://pacificbulbsociety.org/pbswiki/index.php/TulipaSpeciesTwo |publisher=www.pacificbulbsociety.org |access-date=18 September 2017 }}</ref> due to Greig once being president of the Russian Horticultural Society.<ref>{{cite web |title=''Tulipa greigii'' aurea |url=https://www.rareplants.co.uk/product/tulipa-greigii-aurea/ |publisher=rareplants.co.uk |access-date=17 September 2017 }}</ref>

This tulip species was originally found in [[Turkestan]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Liliaceae ''Tulipa greigii'' Regel |url=http://www.ipni.org/ipni/idPlantNameSearch.do?id=542931-1 |access-date=17 September 2017 }}</ref> and then published and described by [[Eduard August von Regel]] in [[Gartenflora]] Vol.22 on page 290 in 1873.<ref name=plantlist/>

== Description ==
''Tulipa greigii'' typically grows {{cvt|8|-|12|inch|cm}} tall, they have single flowers with a bowl-like shape, blooming in early to mid-spring. They also have spotted and striped leaves and the flowers are quite large, up to {{cvt|4|inch|0}} wide. The blooms are more limited in colour shades than with other tulips, ranging from red and yellow to white.<ref>{{cite web |last1=McIntosh |first1=Jamie |title=14 Tulip Varieties to Plant for Spring Blooms |url=https://www.thespruce.com/tulip-types-for-spring-garden-1315804 |website=The Spruce |access-date=17 April 2020 |language=en |date=21 March 2020 }}</ref>

It is known for its variegated green and purple-maroon leaves. Its cultivars 'Oratorio',<ref>{{cite web |title=''Tulipa'' 'Oratorio' (14) |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/58009/i-Tulipa-i-Oratorio-(14)/Details |publisher=The Royal Horticultural Society |access-date=31 August 2020 }}</ref> 'Plaisir',<ref>{{cite web |title=''Tulipa'' 'Plaisir' (14) |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/61718/i-Tulipa-i-Plaisir-(14)/Details |publisher=The Royal Horticultural Society |access-date=31 August 2020 }}</ref> 'Red Riding Hood',<ref>{{cite web |title=''Tulipa'' 'Red Riding Hood' (14) |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/92114/Tulipa-Red-Riding-Hood-(14)/Details |publisher=The Royal Horticultural Society |access-date=31 August 2020 }}</ref> 'Toronto',<ref>{{cite web |title=''Tulipa'' 'Toronto' (14) |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/81418/i-Tulipa-i-Toronto-(14)/Details |publisher=The Royal Horticultural Society |access-date=31 August 2020 }}</ref> and 'United States' have gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web |title=''Tulipa'' 'United States' (14) |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/194542/Tulipa-United-States-(14)/Details |publisher=The Royal Horticultural Society |access-date=31 August 2020 }}</ref>

It was featured on a [[Postage stamps and postal history of Russia|Soviet postage stamp]] in 1960.
